P.s. Nihiyawala, District Bhatinda, Punjab.
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Udit Mathur  Mr. Mohd. Ameen on behalf of  Mr. Vipul Dharnia
For Respondent(s) : Mr. M.S. Bhati, PP with  Mr. C.P. Marwan
Mr. Baltej Singh, for respondent No.2

HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Order 16/11/2023 The instant revision petition has been filed by the petitioner against the order dated 13.09.2021 passed by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge Sangaria, District Hanumangarh in Criminal Case No.05/2019 by which the revision petition filed by the respondent No.2 has been allowed and the matter was remanded back to the learned trial Court for passing a fresh order.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Gurdeep Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2023:Rj-Jd:39261)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: respondent No.2 Darshan Singh has filed protest petition against the Final Report and the learned trial Court i.e. Addl.
Chief Judicial Magistrate Sangaria, Hanumangarh vide his order dated 03.12.2018 accepted the F.R. and rejected the protest petition.

Thereafter the respondent No.2 filed revision petition before the learned Addl. Sessions Judge, Sangaria, District Hanumangarh, who vide impugned order dated 13.09.2021 allowed the revision petition and set aside the order dated 03.12.2018 and remanded the matter back to pass a fresh order in accordance with law.

entities.text: Addl. Sessions Judge, Sangaria, District Hanumangarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The order of the revisional Court is illegal and without considering the material aspect of the case.

In these circumstances, the impugned order dated 13.09.2021 passed by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge,
Sangaria, Hanumangarh may kindly be quashed.

Per contra learned Public Prosecutor and counsel for the respondent No.2 opposed the prayer made by the counsel for the petitioners and submits that the order impugned is merely a remand back order and a fresh order is yet to be passed by the learned trial Court.
Therefore, the revision petition may kindly be dismissed.
I have considered the arguments advanced before me and carefully gone through the material available on record.

Firstly the trial Court accepted the Final Report and rejected the protest petition of the respondent No.2 and thereafter the revisional Court has allowed the revision petition and set aside the [2023:RJ-JD:39261] (3 of 3) [CRLR-420/2022] order of the learned trial Court and case is remanded back for passing a fresh order and upto this time no order has been passed by the learned trial Court.
It is merely a remand back order and no order has been passed by the revisional Court against the present petitioners.

Thus, there is no illegality and infirmity in the impugned order,
hence, no interference is called for from this Court.
Hence, the instant criminal revision petition filed by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.

The learned trial Court is directed to pass a fresh order without prejudice from finding of the learned Addl.
Sessions Judge Sangaria, Hanumangarh.
Stay petition is also decided accordingly.
(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 128-Ishan/-
